title: "I Lift My Banners," Saith the Lord
description: "I Lift My Banners," Saith the Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 29, headed “The ruin of Antichrist, Isa. 63. 4-7”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "I lift my ban-ners," saith the Lord, "Where An-tich-rist has stood, "The cit-y of my gos-pel foes "Shall be a field of blood.

lines: "I lift my banners," saith the Lord,
"The day of my redeem'd is come
"Swift as the lightning it shall move,
"I call for helpers but in vain:
"Well, mine own arm has might enough
While we thy awful vengeance sing,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
